- Implementation requirements owned by another issue or milestone, except prerequisite integration strictly necessary to consume or expose this issue's declared contracts.
- Any scientific redesign, retuning, alternative algorithm, new experiment, convenience feature, compatibility shim, or post-hoc behavior not required by the mapped roadmap authority.
- Moving unfinished in-scope work into documentation, TODOs, follow-up issues, or downstream implementation merely to close this issue.

# M06 — I33 Implement Paired Statistical Inference and Canonical Comparison Registry

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M06 — Collapse Experiments and Resolved Core
- **Primary deliverable:** Implement seed-level pairing, exact sign-flip superiority/non-inferiority tests, Holm families, effects, bootstrap confidence intervals, materiality, failed-pair rules, and canonical comparison identities.
- **Issue type:** Implementation

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §18
- §18.1
- §18.2
- §18.3
- §18.4
- §18.5
- §18.6
- §18.8
- §18.9
- §18.9 Family 10

### Requirements

- **Implementation requirements:** REQ-0931–REQ-0957; REQ-0959–REQ-0969; REQ-0996–REQ-1019; REQ-2105–REQ-2106
- **Preserved non-implementation constraints:** REQ-0958

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue traces to the roadmap authority and inventory requirements listed above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy them.

## Objective

Implement seed-level pairing, exact sign-flip superiority/non-inferiority tests, Holm families, effects, bootstrap confidence intervals, materiality, failed-pair rules, and canonical comparison identities.

## Scope

Implement only the following roadmap/inventory requirements. Each bullet is an explicit implementation obligation; none may remain implicit in tests or downstream work.

- **REQ-0931 — §18 — Configuration:** `metrics_and_statistics.*` may contain only numerical aggregation/statistical parameters, materiality/completion thresholds, and publication-format values; inferential resampling seed comes from `seeds_and_determinism.analysis_seed`.
- **REQ-0932 — §18 — Configuration:** Test definitions, sidedness, quantile/resampling semantics, multiplicity families/method, tie rules, and collapse/survival actions must be fixed by Section 18 rather than configurable procedure strings.
- **REQ-0933 — §18.1 — Statistical Analysis:** The independent confirmatory experimental unit must be the master-seed scenario instance, with 10 planned master seeds.
- **REQ-0934 — §18.1 — Statistical Analysis:** The pairing key must be exactly `(dataset, experiment_name, scientific_scenario, master_seed)`.
- **REQ-0935 — §18.1 — Statistical Analysis:** Methods compared within a scenario must share source/domain/attack/evidence-role seeds.
- **REQ-0936 — §18.1 — Statistical Analysis:** Domain rows within a seed must not be treated as independent samples.
- **REQ-0937 — §18.2 — Statistical Analysis:** Paired superiority comparisons must use a two-sided exact paired sign-flip permutation test on seed-level differences.
- **REQ-0938 — §18.2 — Statistical Analysis:** For `n=10`, the superiority test must enumerate all 1024 sign assignments.
- **REQ-0939 — §18.2 — Statistical Analysis:** The superiority statistic must be mean paired difference and exact p-value must count permutations with absolute mean at least the observed absolute mean divided by `2^n`.
- **REQ-0940 — §18.2 — Statistical Analysis:** Zero paired differences must remain in the vector and must not be discarded.
- **REQ-0941 — §18.2 — Statistical Analysis:** Directional non-inferiority with benefit-oriented difference `d=method-reference` and degradation margin `m>0` must test the one-sided null mean difference `<=-m` via exact sign-flip permutations on `d+m`.
- **REQ-0942 — §18.2 — Statistical Analysis:** The statistical artifact must record the exact non-inferiority null orientation.
- **REQ-0943 — §18.3 — Configuration:** Family-wise alpha must be 0.05.
- **REQ-0944 — §18.3 — Statistical Analysis:** Multiplicity correction must be Holm step-down within each predefined claim family, with raw-p ties ordered by canonical comparison name.
- **REQ-0945 — §18.3 — Statistical Analysis:** There must be no global correction across unrelated claim families.
- **REQ-0946 — §18.3 — Statistical Analysis:** Both raw and Holm-adjusted p-values must be stored.
- **REQ-0947 — §18.3 — Statistical Analysis:** The claim-family registry must contain exactly: proposal-screen necessity; plurality necessity; source-exclusion central claim; external reproduction verification necessity; primary baseline superiority; reproducer robustness; verifier robustness; mechanism ablation; heterogeneity/failure-boundary secondary comparisons; secondary generalization.
- **REQ-0948 — §18.4 — Statistical Analysis:** Every paired comparison must report mean paired difference in native units.
- **REQ-0949 — §18.4 — Statistical Analysis:** Every paired comparison must report median paired difference.
- **REQ-0950 — §18.4 — Statistical Analysis:** Every paired comparison must report paired standardized effect `d_z=mean(d)/sample_SD(d)` with `ddof=1`.
- **REQ-0951 — §18.4 — Statistical Analysis:** If paired-difference SD is zero, `d_z` must be +INF/-INF for nonzero mean by sign and 0 when all differences are zero; no finite substitute is allowed.
- **REQ-0952 — §18.5 — Statistical Analysis:** Mean paired-difference confidence intervals must be 95% percentile bootstrap intervals.
- **REQ-0953 — §18.5 — Statistical Analysis:** Bootstrap resampling unit must be a complete master-seed pair.
- **REQ-0954 — §18.5 — Configuration:** Bootstrap must use exactly 10,000 resamples.
- **REQ-0955 — §18.5 — Configuration:** Bootstrap seed must be exactly 424242.
- **REQ-0956 — §18.5 — Statistical Analysis:** Each bootstrap sample must contain the number of complete pairs, sampled with replacement.
- **REQ-0957 — §18.5 — Statistical Analysis:** CI endpoints must be 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles using type-7/linear interpolation.
- **REQ-0959 — §18.6 — Configuration:** Target-F1 material gain threshold must be +0.02 absolute.
- **REQ-0960 — §18.6 — Configuration:** Supported macro-F1 non-inferiority margin must allow no worse than -0.02 absolute degradation.
- **REQ-0961 — §18.6 — Configuration:** Benign-FAR non-inferiority margin must allow no worse than +0.01 absolute increase.
- **REQ-0962 — §18.6 — Configuration:** Source-exclusion ASR material reduction must be at least 0.20 absolute.
- **REQ-0963 — §18.6 — Configuration:** Malicious-admission material reduction must be at least 0.10 absolute.
- **REQ-0964 — §18.6 — Configuration:** Legitimate-admission non-inferiority margin must be 0.05 absolute.
- **REQ-0965 — §18.6 — Configuration:** Worst-domain target-F1 material gain must be at least 0.05 absolute.
- **REQ-0966 — §18.6 — Configuration:** False-launch material reduction must be at least 0.15 absolute.
- **REQ-0967 — §18.6 — Configuration:** Reproduction-attempt material reduction must be at least 25% relative.
- **REQ-0968 — §18.6 — Configuration:** Post-evidence-overhead material reduction must be at least 20% relative.
- **REQ-0969 — §18.6 — Statistical Analysis:** A relative reduction whose reference value is 0 is undefined and must not be the sole support criterion.
- **REQ-2105 — §18.6 — Statistical Analysis:** A claim may be supported only when both its predeclared inferential rule and its practical materiality rule are satisfied.
- **REQ-0996 — §18.8 — Failure Semantics:** A technical run may receive at most one same-cell-phase infrastructure retry.
- **REQ-0997 — §18.8 — Failure Semantics:** After the single allowed retry fails, the planned seed must remain technically missing and must never be replaced by another seed.
- **REQ-0998 — §18.8 — Reporting:** Technical failures must appear in all run-count and reporting tables.
- **REQ-0999 — §18.8 — Statistical Analysis:** A paired comparison with 10 or 9 complete seed pairs must analyze complete pairs and report exact `n`.
- **REQ-1000 — §18.8 — Statistical Analysis:** A paired comparison with fewer than 9 complete pairs must be `Inconclusive Technical` and must not support a claim.
- **REQ-1001 — §18.8 — Statistical Analysis:** No imputation or seed replacement is allowed for incomplete paired comparisons.
- **REQ-1002 — §18.8 — Statistical Analysis:** Scientifically infeasible cells caused by insufficient evidence are valid outcomes; terminal binary metrics may remain defined while impossible continuous metrics are `NA` with reason.
- **REQ-1003 — §18.8 — Statistical Analysis:** Multiplicity families must be declared before execution.
- **REQ-1004 — §18.8 — Statistical Analysis:** A predeclared family member that becomes technically inconclusive/undefined must remain in the family manifest with raw p-value 1.0 for Holm adjustment only and must not support a claim.
- **REQ-1005 — §18.8 — Statistical Analysis:** Structurally not-applicable metrics by experiment definition must not be family members.
- **REQ-1006 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Only comparisons generated by the Section 18.9 registry may be claim-bearing inferential tests; other displayed differences are descriptive unless explicitly linked to a registry rule.
- **REQ-1007 — §18.9 — Artifact:** Canonical comparison names must be `{family}\|{experiment}\|{scenario}\|{method}__vs__{reference}\|{metric}\|{test_kind}`.
- **REQ-1008 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Benefit-oriented differences must be method-reference for higher-is-better outcomes and reference-method for lower-is-better outcomes (ASR, MAR, supported harm, benign-FAR increase, false launch, attempts, overhead).
- **REQ-1009 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Superiority must use the two-sided exact sign-flip p-value plus expected sign/materiality; non-inferiority must use the one-sided shifted sign-flip test.
- **REQ-1010 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 1 proposal-screen necessity comparison registry must be exactly: Proposal-Assisted vs Candidate-Free must test false-launch superiority on Generic Hard Supported and Irrelevant Source Improvement; attempts and overhead superiority on all four Section 30.4 episodes; LAR non-inferiority on Legitimate Target; MAR non-inferiority on Useful Backdoored Source. Only the first three effect types can positively support survival.
- **REQ-1011 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 2 plurality necessity comparison registry must be exactly: Full Plurality vs One Independent Retrain must test MAR where defined and worst-domain target-F1 in Honest Site-Specific Feature Shift —1.0 and One Byzantine Source-Copy; LAR/supported-harm are full-precision constraints.
- **REQ-1012 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 3 source exclusion comparison registry must be exactly: Full FedSIRA vs Source-Update Sanitization on Useful Backdoored Source —5% must use ASR as sole superiority test, with target-F1/support/benign constraints.
- **REQ-1013 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 4 external verification comparison registry must be exactly: Full FedSIRA vs Multiple Retrains with Direct Krum must test MAR where defined and worst-domain target-F1 in site-shift, Source-Copy, and Verifier-Aware conditions; Legitimate Transferable supplies only LAR constraint.
- **REQ-1014 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 5 primary baselines comparison registry must be exactly: Resolved FedSIRA must be compared to each of 13 non-FedSIRA methods in each primary scenario for target-F1 superiority, applicable LAR/support/benign non-inferiority, applicable MAR superiority, and applicable ASR superiority, all in one Holm family.
- **REQ-1015 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 6 reproducer robustness comparison registry must be exactly: Within each non-CLEAN robustness condition, Resolved FedSIRA must compare against One Retrain, Direct Krum, and Krum Reference for applicable MAR, target F1, and trigger ASR; CLEAN uses LAR/target-F1 non-inferiority.
- **REQ-1016 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 7 verifier robustness comparison registry must be exactly: False-positive conditions must compare MAR deterioration vs All Honest; false-negative conditions must compare LAR non-inferiority vs All Honest; random contamination frequency is descriptive.
- **REQ-1017 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 8 mechanism ablation comparison registry must be exactly: Every Section 30.10 variant must use a matched Full FedSIRA reference and its declared primary metric; invalid three-row Krum has no p-value, while the labeled coordinate-median diagnostic supplies the comparison metric.
- **REQ-1018 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 9 failure/heterogeneity comparison registry must be exactly: Must include only shared-epistemic corrupted-vs-matched-clean metrics, broad-contract false-equivalence vs all-zero reference for each mixture, and each method non-Natural heterogeneity regime vs Natural for LAR and worst-domain target F1.
- **REQ-1019 — §18.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Family 10 secondary generalization comparison registry must be exactly: For both secondary scenarios, Resolved FedSIRA vs One Retrain and Direct Krum must test one-sided target-F1 non-inferiority margin 0.02 and applicable MAR non-inferiority margin 0.05 in one Holm family.
- **REQ-2106 — §18.9 Family 10 — Statistical Analysis:** For every applicable Family 10 secondary-generalization comparison, the Holm-adjusted p-value must be `<0.05` in addition to satisfying the stated non-inferiority material margin.

# M06 — I34 Implement Mechanical Collapse Survival Rules and Resolved-Core Decision Logic

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M06 — Collapse Experiments and Resolved Core
- **Primary deliverable:** Implement preregistered survival rules for proposal assistance, plurality, direct source exclusion, and external verification plus the complete eight-case mechanical resolved-core mapping.
- **Issue type:** Implementation

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §6.4
- §18.7 Proposal
- §18.7 Plurality
- §18.7 Source exclusion
- §18.7 External verification
- §18.7 Resolved core
- §18.7 Resolved core mapping

### Requirements

- **Implementation requirements:** REQ-0970–REQ-0978; REQ-0980–REQ-0983; REQ-0985–REQ-0994
- **Preserved non-implementation constraints:** REQ-0196; REQ-0979; REQ-0984; REQ-0995

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue traces to the roadmap authority and inventory requirements listed above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy them.

## Objective

Implement preregistered survival rules for proposal assistance, plurality, direct source exclusion, and external verification plus the complete eight-case mechanical resolved-core mapping.

## Scope

Implement only the following roadmap/inventory requirements. Each bullet is an explicit implementation obligation; none may remain implicit in tests or downstream work.

- **REQ-0970 — §18.7 Proposal — Statistical Analysis:** Proposal assistance may survive only if at least one of false-launch reduction≥0.15, reproduction-attempt reduction≥25%, or post-evidence-overhead reduction≥20% has Holm-adjusted p<0.05 and meets materiality.
- **REQ-0971 — §18.7 Proposal — Statistical Analysis:** Proposal assistance survival additionally requires legitimate-admission degradation≤0.05.
- **REQ-0972 — §18.7 Proposal — Statistical Analysis:** Proposal assistance survival additionally requires malicious-admission rate to worsen by no more than 0.02 absolute.
- **REQ-0973 — §18.7 Proposal — Algorithm:** If proposal survival fails, the resolved core must use candidate-free opening and retain proposal assistance only as a reported negative/diagnostic result.
- **REQ-0974 — §18.7 Plurality — Statistical Analysis:** Plurality may survive only if, versus `One Independent Retrain`, at least one preregistered site-specific-overfit or Byzantine-reproducer condition shows MAR reduction≥0.10 or worst-domain target-F1 gain≥0.05 with Holm-adjusted p<0.05.
- **REQ-0975 — §18.7 Plurality — Statistical Analysis:** Plurality survival requires legitimate-admission degradation≤0.05 and supported macro-F1 harm within 0.02.
- **REQ-0976 — §18.7 Plurality — Algorithm:** If plurality survival fails, the single-reproduction path must become the simplest surviving core path.
- **REQ-0977 — §18.7 Source exclusion — Statistical Analysis:** Direct source exclusion may survive only against `Source-Update Sanitization Reference` in `Useful+Backdoor` when ASR decreases by at least 0.20 with adjusted p<0.05.
- **REQ-0978 — §18.7 Source exclusion — Statistical Analysis:** Direct source-exclusion survival requires target F1 non-inferiority within 0.02 and supported macro-F1/benign FAR to satisfy the Capability Claim Contract.
- **REQ-0980 — §18.7 External verification — Statistical Analysis:** External reproduction verification may survive only versus `Multiple Retrains with Direct Krum` when at least one preregistered failure condition has MAR reduction≥0.10 or worst-domain target-F1 gain≥0.05 with adjusted p<0.05.
- **REQ-0981 — §18.7 External verification — Statistical Analysis:** External-verification survival requires legitimate-admission degradation≤0.05.
- **REQ-0982 — §18.7 External verification — Algorithm:** If external-verification survival fails, external/cross-verification must be removed from the simplest surviving core.
- **REQ-0983 — §18.7 Resolved core — Artifact:** After all four collapse decision artifacts exist, `experiments/collapse.py` must deterministically create one `Resolved FedSIRA Core` artifact with no manual operator choice or outcome-dependent redesign.
- **REQ-0985 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** For `P pass, R pass, V pass`, the resolved core must use opening `proposal-assisted`, reproduction requirement `first 5 certified non-source rows`, row verification `ordinary 3-verifier 2-of-3 per row`, production update `Krum over first 5 certified rows`, and always require the final fresh gate.
- **REQ-0986 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** For `P fail, R pass, V pass`, the resolved core must use opening `candidate-free`, reproduction requirement `first 5 certified non-source rows`, row verification `ordinary 3-verifier 2-of-3 per row`, production update `Krum over first 5 certified rows`, and always require the final fresh gate.
- **REQ-0987 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** For `P pass, R pass, V fail`, the resolved core must use opening `proposal-assisted`, reproduction requirement `first 5 adequate committed non-source rows`, row verification `none`, production update `Krum over first 5 committed rows`, and always require the final fresh gate.
- **REQ-0988 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** For `P fail, R pass, V fail`, the resolved core must use opening `candidate-free`, reproduction requirement `first 5 adequate committed non-source rows`, row verification `none`, production update `Krum over first 5 committed rows`, and always require the final fresh gate.
- **REQ-0989 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** For `P pass, R fail, V pass`, the resolved core must use opening `proposal-assisted`, reproduction requirement `first adequate non-source row passing one fresh verifier`, row verification `one first-adequate eligible post-commitment verifier; Positive required`, production update `that reproduction update directly`, and always require the final fresh gate.
- **REQ-0990 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** For `P fail, R fail, V pass`, the resolved core must use opening `candidate-free`, reproduction requirement `first adequate non-source row passing one fresh verifier`, row verification `same one-verifier rule`, production update `that reproduction update directly`, and always require the final fresh gate.
- **REQ-0991 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** For `P pass, R fail, V fail`, the resolved core must use opening `proposal-assisted`, reproduction requirement `first adequate committed non-source row`, row verification `none`, production update `that reproduction update directly`, and always require the final fresh gate.
- **REQ-0992 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** For `P fail, R fail, V fail`, the resolved core must use opening `candidate-free`, reproduction requirement `first adequate committed non-source row`, row verification `none`, production update `that reproduction update directly`, and always require the final fresh gate.
- **REQ-0993 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** On a one-verifier resolved path, inadequate verifier opportunities must be skipped without a vote; no adequate verifier yields `Dormant`; an adequate negative rejects that row and scanning continues; first positive verified row becomes production update.
- **REQ-0994 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping — Algorithm:** `Synthesis Pending` must be interpreted generically as production update ready for final gate, and Krum-specific invariants apply only when plurality survives.

### Preserved Non-Implementation Constraints

These constraints create no separate implementation work, but this issue must not violate them:

- **REQ-0196 — §6.4:** Proposal assistance, plurality, or external verification may be removed only by the Section 18.7 mechanical survival rules; a negative source-exclusion result must never authorize direct source deployment.
- **REQ-0979 — §18.7 Source exclusion:** Failure of the direct source-exclusion gate must mark the central contribution `Not Supported`; later robustness cells must not override that gate.
- **REQ-0984 — §18.7 Resolved core:** Failure of the direct source-exclusion performance gate must not authorize source deployment; the resolved characterization path remains source-excluded.
- **REQ-0995 — §18.7 Resolved core mapping:** The Section 18.7 mapping is the sole authority for post-collapse ablations and downstream resolved-core experiment cells.

# M06 — I35 Implement Experiment Planner, Runner, Execution Order, and Cell Registry

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M06 — Collapse Experiments and Resolved Core
- **Primary deliverable:** Implement read-only planning, exact-name experiment execution, dependency-ordered workflow, semantic cell enumeration/counts, completion accounting, reuse/recovery, and invalid-baseline preservation.
- **Issue type:** Infrastructure

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §24.3
- §24.5
- §29
- §30
- §31

### Requirements

- **Implementation requirements:** REQ-1537–REQ-1540; REQ-1545–REQ-1557; REQ-1760–REQ-1777; REQ-1780–REQ-1782; REQ-1914–REQ-1939; REQ-2203
- **Preserved non-implementation constraints:** REQ-1558; REQ-1778–REQ-1779

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue traces to the roadmap authority and inventory requirements listed above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy them.

## Objective

Implement read-only planning, exact-name experiment execution, dependency-ordered workflow, semantic cell enumeration/counts, completion accounting, reuse/recovery, and invalid-baseline preservation.

## Scope

Implement only the following roadmap/inventory requirements. Each bullet is an explicit implementation obligation; none may remain implicit in tests or downstream work.

- **REQ-1537 — §24.3 — CLI / Execution:** `plan` must be read-only.
- **REQ-1538 — §24.3 — CLI / Execution:** `plan` must resolve canonical experiment order, dependencies, datasets, methods, conditions, seeds, Section 31 counts, blocked conditions, matched-reference prerequisites, and reusable artifact families.
- **REQ-1539 — §24.3 — CLI / Execution:** Before collapse completion, `plan` must show post-core cells as dependent on unresolved core; after all four decisions, it must show the mechanically derived core mapping.
- **REQ-1540 — §24.3 — CLI / Execution:** `plan` must not create a user-managed plan and must not accept overwrite.
- **REQ-1545 — §24.5 — CLI / Execution:** `run <experiment name>` must accept only exact descriptive Section 30 experiment names.
- **REQ-1546 — §24.5 — CLI / Execution:** One `run` invocation must own prerequisite validation, planned cell execution, metrics, statistical analysis, CIs/effects, multiplicity, scientific gates, invariant/provenance verification, and experiment completion.
- **REQ-1547 — §24.5 — Artifact:** Before each cell, `run` must resolve the artifact DAG and reuse matching data/splits/scalers/anchors/source/reproduction checkpoints/scores/calibrations/verifier/final-gate intermediates even across experiments.
- **REQ-1548 — §24.5 — Provenance:** Experiment identity may enter an artifact fingerprint only when the experiment definition changes the artifact's scientific semantics.
- **REQ-1549 — §24.5 — CLI / Execution:** Once the fourth collapse decision is complete, `run` must materialize/validate the deterministic Resolved FedSIRA Core artifact.
- **REQ-1550 — §24.5 — Failure Semantics:** Post-core experiments must refuse execution when the Resolved FedSIRA Core prerequisite is absent or stale.
- **REQ-1551 — §24.5 — Artifact:** A later cell failure must not invalidate already completed independent cells or shared upstream artifacts.
- **REQ-1552 — §24.5 — Artifact:** After correction, `run` must recompute only the first affected artifact and descendants; metric corrections may reuse scores, scoring corrections checkpoints, training corrections prepared data/unaffected anchors, and reporting corrections all scientific computation.
- **REQ-1553 — §24.5 — CLI / Execution:** Analysis/statistics/protocol verification must be internal to `run`; there must be no separate public analysis/verification command.
- **REQ-1554 — §24.5 — Failure Semantics:** A scientifically unfavorable/null result must still complete as `Completed`; technical execution failure is `Failed`; leakage/invariant/provenance/authoritative-config violation is `Invalid`.
- **REQ-1555 — §24.5 — CLI / Execution:** If all required artifacts are already validly complete, `run` must return an already-completed success and create no duplicate observation.
- **REQ-1556 — §24.5 — CLI / Execution:** `run --overwrite` must recompute experiment-owned artifacts under the same scientific contract without recursively rebuilding compatible shared prerequisites.
- **REQ-1557 — §24.5 — Artifact:** Overwrite replacements must be staged and atomically activated; unchanged identity preserves descendants, changed identity stales only descendants.

## Out of Scope

- Implementation requirements owned by another issue or milestone, except prerequisite integration strictly necessary to consume or expose this issue's declared contracts.
- Any scientific redesign, retuning, alternative algorithm, new experiment, convenience feature, compatibility shim, or post-hoc behavior not required by the mapped roadmap authority.
- Moving unfinished in-scope work into documentation, TODOs, follow-up issues, or downstream implementation merely to close this issue.

## Dependencies

### Blocked By

- M01 — I08 Implement CLI Foundation, Doctor, and Generic Artifact Validation — uses CLI routing, diagnostics, reuse, and overwrite semantics.
- M02 — I13 Implement Data and Domain Validation Test Gate — requires the blocking data/domain evidence gate.
- M03 — I18 Validate Model, FL, Metric, and Statistical Numerics — requires model/metric numerical validation.
- M04 — I26 Implement Protocol Smoke, Invariant, and Mathematical Validation Gate — requires the blocking protocol invariant gate.
- M05 — I32 Execute Baseline Implementation Validation — requires baseline implementation validation.
- M06 — I33 Implement Paired Statistical Inference and Canonical Comparison Registry — uses canonical comparison identities and completion semantics.

- M06 — I37 Run Single-Reproduction Necessity Experiment — Provides the prerequisite for this downstream contract: uses the preregistered planner/runner and exact semantic-cell registry.
- M06 — I38 Run Source-Artifact Exclusion Necessity Experiment — Provides the prerequisite for this downstream contract: uses the preregistered planner/runner and exact semantic-cell registry.
- M06 — I39 Run External Verification Necessity Experiment — Provides the prerequisite for this downstream contract: uses the preregistered planner/runner and exact semantic-cell registry.

Dependencies are satisfied only by valid, provenance-compatible, non-stale evidence or interfaces. An issue number alone is never sufficient.

## Non-Negotiable Implementation Contracts

The implementation must preserve exactly, where defined by the roadmap:

- roadmap-defined algorithmic semantics;
- formulas, thresholds, equality semantics, tolerances, and numerical conventions;
- configuration authority and ownership;
- dataset, split, eligibility, chronology, and preprocessing semantics;
- experiment coordinates, controls, comparators, seeds, and statistical procedures;
- deterministic and reproducibility requirements;
- failure, unavailable, infeasible, insufficient-evidence, suppression, and abstention semantics;
- artifact, integrity, completion, and provenance requirements;
- scientific claim boundaries.

Do not introduce:

- undocumented defaults;
- hidden fallbacks;
- alternative algorithms or scientific behavior;
- post-hoc scientific choices;
- duplicated scientific constants;
- silent compatibility behavior;
- agent-invented values or assumptions.

If the roadmap is genuinely missing or contradictory on a decision that materially affects scientific or implementation behavior, do not guess. Record it under **Roadmap Deviations / Follow-Ups** and create a dedicated clarification or correction issue.

### Issue-Specific Constraint Verification

- [ ] **REQ-1558:** The implementation and its outputs preserve this boundary exactly: `--overwrite` must never create a second logical scientific observation.
- [ ] **REQ-1778:** The implementation and its outputs preserve this boundary exactly: A valid null/boundary result must not become software failure and must not trigger retuning.
- [ ] **REQ-1779:** The implementation and its outputs preserve this boundary exactly: A collapse gate rejecting a central mechanism claim may not be resurrected by later favorable characterization.

## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Roadmap-declared production modules responsible for implement experiment planner, runner, execution order, and cell registry.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Existing authoritative configuration/domain models consumed read-only; no new scientific defaults or duplicated constants.
- Typed statuses/reasons/outcomes preserving failure, invalid, unavailable, insufficient-evidence, Dormant, Rejected Claim, Expired, and related distinctions where applicable.

### CLI / Application Surface

- The exact public CLI/application commands and routing behavior named by the mapped requirements; CLI remains a thin boundary.

### Tests

- Unit and integration tests directly exercising every acceptance criterion and nearest boundary/failure case.
- Regression tests for any defect found while implementing this issue.
- Serialization, checksum/corruption, stale-evidence, dependency-fingerprint, reuse/rebuild, and provenance-validation fixtures.
- Planner/cell-enumeration and small representative end-to-end/smoke fixtures proving the exact preregistered execution path.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Roadmap-declared machine-readable artifacts/manifests/checkpoints/digests owned by this issue, published atomically with schema/integrity/provenance.
- Complete terminal cell records, metrics/statistics/decision evidence, manifests, and experiment completion evidence for the mapped experiment scope.

Exact file placement follows the repository architecture unless a mapped requirement explicitly mandates a path.

## Required Tests

The following categories are mandatory to evaluate for this issue. A genuinely inapplicable category must be recorded as `N/A — <reason>` in the completion record rather than silently ignored.

- [ ] Unit tests
- [ ] Boundary and edge-case tests
- [ ] Invalid-input and failure-path tests
- [ ] Numerical / formula tests where scientific calculations are involved
- [ ] Determinism / reproducibility tests where stochastic or deterministic behavior is specified
- [ ] Serialization / integrity / corruption tests where persisted artifacts are involved
- [ ] Provenance / stale-evidence tests where evidence dependencies are involved
- [ ] Resume / reuse / rebuild tests where execution state is involved
- [ ] Integration tests
- [ ] CLI / end-to-end tests where an execution surface is involved
- [ ] Smoke tests where the real execution path must be exercised cheaply
- [ ] Regression tests for every bug discovered while implementing this issue

Each test must prove an acceptance criterion, invariant, failure path, or previously observed defect. Avoid tests that merely duplicate implementation details.

## Required Outputs

- **REQ-1822 — §30.9 — Experiment:** `Primary Confirmatory Evaluation` must be class `Confirmatory` with exactly `14 methods × 3 scenarios × 10 seeds = 420` cells.
- **REQ-1823 — §30.9 — Experiment:** Primary confirmatory method registry must be exactly: Resolved FedSIRA Core, FedAvg Reference, Client Review with Direct Source Admission, Client Review then One Independent Retrain, One Independent Retrain, Multiple Retrains with Direct Krum, Multiple-Model Certified Ensemble, Independent Local Reference with Source Admission, Update Reconstruction Filter, Density-Cluster Trimmed Mean, Secure Continual Assessment Reference, Recovery after Source Admission, Source-Update Sanitization Reference, Krum Robust Aggregation Reference.

- **REQ-1830 — §30.9 — Statistical Analysis:** Statistics must use exactly Section 18 with no new tests; claims require both statistical and materiality conditions.

# M07 — I42 Run Mechanism Ablation Program

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M07 — Confirmatory and Boundary Evidence Program
- **Primary deliverable:** Execute all eighteen preregistered mechanism-ablation variants with matched Full FedSIRA references and preserve confirmatory versus diagnostic interpretation.
- **Issue type:** Experiment

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §30.10

### Requirements

- **Implementation requirements:** REQ-1831–REQ-1857
- **Preserved non-implementation constraints:** REQ-1858

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue traces to the roadmap authority and inventory requirements listed above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy them.

## Objective

Execute all eighteen preregistered mechanism-ablation variants with matched Full FedSIRA references and preserve confirmatory versus diagnostic interpretation.

## Scope

Implement only the following roadmap/inventory requirements. Each bullet is an explicit implementation obligation; none may remain implicit in tests or downstream work.

- **REQ-1831 — §30.10 — Experiment:** `Mechanism Ablation` must be class `Ablation` with exactly `18 variants × 10 seeds = 180` semantic cells.
- **REQ-1832 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Every non-Full-FedSIRA ablation must consume a matched Full FedSIRA reference with identical scenario, seed, source, roles, attack/heterogeneity transforms, and non-ablated settings; identical references may be reused/materialized as shared prerequisites without adding experiment cells.
- **REQ-1833 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Full FedSIRA` must implement `complete Sections 7.1–7.7 multi-reproduction path`, use scenario `Useful Backdoored Source —5%`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `reference ASR`.
- **REQ-1834 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `No Proposal Screen` must implement `candidate-free opening; downstream complete path`, use scenario `Mixed Legitimate/Irrelevant Proposal Episode`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `reproduction attempts`.
- **REQ-1835 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Raw Target-F1 Screen Only` must implement `screen positive by target gain≥0.20 + supported constraints; no loss differential/matching`, use scenario `Generic Hard Supported Examples`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `false launch rate`.
- **REQ-1836 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `No Matched Control` must implement `use ΔM≥0.05 plus target/support conditions; omit ΔC`, use scenario `Generic Hard Supported Examples`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `false launch rate`.
- **REQ-1837 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Source Release after Peer Review` must implement `deploy source after 2-of-3 review`, use scenario `Useful Backdoored Source —5%`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `ASR`.
- **REQ-1838 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Source Release after Full External Check` must implement `source itself receives one ordinary 3-verifier panel + final gate, then source deployed; no fabricated independent rows`, use scenario `Useful Backdoored Source —5%`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `ASR`.
- **REQ-1839 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `One Independent Reproduction` must implement `first clean reproduction + one fresh verifier + final gate`, use scenario `Honest Site-Specific Feature Shift —1.0`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `worst-domain target F1`.
- **REQ-1840 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Multiple Reproductions without Cross-Verification` must implement `first five adequate committed rows → Krum → final gate`, use scenario `One Malicious Reproducer`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `MAR`.
- **REQ-1841 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Same-Context Verification Only` must implement `choose three adequate eligible verifiers closest by anchor-train feature-mean distance`, use scenario `Natural`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `LAR`.
- **REQ-1842 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `No Origin Exclusion` must implement `source may occupy first reproduction slot and verify other rows but not self-verify`, use scenario `Useful Backdoored Source —5%`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `ASR`.
- **REQ-1843 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Parameter-Similarity Certification` must implement `Section 16.5 cosine certification; no functional Capability Claim Contract verifier`, use scenario `Feature Shift ±1.0`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `LAR`.
- **REQ-1844 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Candidate-Free Reproduction` must implement `candidate-free opening; otherwise complete path`, use scenario `Legitimate Target Capability`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `post-evidence overhead`.
- **REQ-1845 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Direct Krum of Retrains` must implement `same reproduction opportunities, no external verification`, use scenario `One Verifier-Aware Backdoor Reproducer`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `MAR`.
- **REQ-1846 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Generic Three-Row Threshold` must implement `Krum n=3,f=1 branch Invalid; separately execute 3-row coordinate median`, use scenario `One Malicious Reproducer`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `coordinate-median MAR`.
- **REQ-1847 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Random Committee Profile` must implement `Section 13.7 random verifier profile with one compromised false-positive verifier`, use scenario `One Compromised Verifier`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `MAR`.
- **REQ-1848 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `No Final Synthesis Gate` must implement `after Krum admit immediately without final fresh evidence`, use scenario `Feature Shift ±1.0`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `worst-domain target F1`.
- **REQ-1849 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Byzantine Reproducer Copies Source` must implement `force one reproduction row to exact source update`, use scenario `Useful Backdoored Source —5%`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `ASR`.
- **REQ-1850 — §30.10 — Ablation:** Ablation `Capability-Contract Granularity` must implement `execute broad/A/B scoped contracts on root-cause fixture`, use scenario `Under-Specification Fixture`, and use claim-bearing primary metric `broad false-same-capability certification rate`.
- **REQ-1851 — §30.10 — Ablation:** `Mixed Legitimate/Irrelevant Proposal Episode` must contain exactly two claim instances per master seed; attempts/overhead are arithmetic means, LAR only from legitimate instance, false launch only from irrelevant instance.
- **REQ-1852 — §30.10 — Ablation:** `One Malicious Reproducer` must mean one Model-Replacement attacker on a clean Legitimate Target background.
- **REQ-1853 — §30.10 — Ablation:** `Natural` must mean clean Legitimate Target, all-honest participants, Natural heterogeneity.
- **REQ-1854 — §30.10 — Ablation:** `Feature Shift ±1.0`/Honest Site-Specific Feature Shift —1.0 must mean all-honest Legitimate Target with Section 15.9 ±1.0 transform.
- **REQ-1855 — §30.10 — Ablation:** `One Compromised Verifier` must mean one False Positive verifier plus exactly one Model-Replacement reproduction row, all others honest.
- **REQ-1856 — §30.10 — Ablation:** `Under-Specification Fixture` must use the Balanced 50/50 mixture.
- **REQ-1857 — §30.10 — Experiment:** All ablation variants must also report target F1 and supported harm; Family 8 governs statistics; Full FedSIRA has no self-comparison p-value.

- **REQ-1872 — §30.12 — Experiment:** Primary metrics are MAR for false-positive cases and LAR/dormancy for false-negative cases; secondary metrics verification yield, verifier abstention, random-panel contamination frequency.

Execute admission-delay decomposition and descriptive resource/communication/timing measurements, separating information-arrival cost from protocol overhead.

## Scope

Implement only the following roadmap/inventory requirements. Each bullet is an explicit implementation obligation; none may remain implicit in tests or downstream work.

- **REQ-0058 — §2 — Experiment:** Research-question contract — Evidence-arrival versus protocol delay: `Admission-Delay Decomposition` and `Efficiency Measurement` must separate evidence-arrival delay from post-evidence overhead.
- **REQ-1895 — §30.18 — Experiment:** `Admission-Delay Decomposition` must be class `Diagnostic` with exactly `3 methods × 4 schedules × 10 seeds = 120` cells.
- **REQ-1896 — §30.18 — Experiment:** Methods must be Resolved FedSIRA, One Independent Retrain, Multiple Retrains with Direct Krum; schedules all four Section 15.8 schedules.
- **REQ-1897 — §30.18 — Experiment:** Metrics must be T_evidence logical cycles, wall-clock post-evidence components, total attempts, terminal state.
- **REQ-1899 — §30.19 — Experiment:** `Efficiency Measurement` must be class `Diagnostic` with exactly `4 methods × 3 master seeds × 5 timing repetitions = 60` cells.
- **REQ-1900 — §30.19 — Experiment:** Methods must be Resolved FedSIRA, One Independent Retrain, Multiple Retrains with Direct Krum, Client Review with Direct Source Admission; seeds only 1103,1217,1321; exactly five repetitions per method-seed.
- **REQ-1902 — §30.19 — Artifact:** Each repetition must run in a dedicated single-process timing worker and write under `outputs/experiments/Efficiency Measurement/diagnostics/runtime/repetitions/<method>/<master-seed>/<repetition-index>/`; repetition payloads must never be reusable scientific parents.
- **REQ-1903 — §30.19 — Metric:** Persistent storage bytes per repetition must recursively sum regular-file sizes in that repetition directory excluding symlinks/references to shared inputs.
- **REQ-1904 — §30.19 — Reproducibility:** Before each timed repetition: load preprocessed data, synchronize CUDA, run one unreported warm-up forward pass, clear CUDA peak-memory counters, do not clear OS filesystem cache, and ensure no concurrent scientific GPU job.
- **REQ-1905 — §30.19 — Statistical Analysis:** Report median and IQR across five repetitions per seed, then descriptive median across three seed medians; do not run significance tests on timing repetitions.
- **REQ-1906 — §30.19 — Experiment:** Efficiency metrics must include wall-clock, GPU time, peak GPU memory, host RSS, communication bytes, transmissions, and storage.

### Preserved Non-Implementation Constraints

These constraints create no separate implementation work, but this issue must not violate them:

- **REQ-1898 — §30.18:** T_evidence must never be reported as FedSIRA compute overhead.
- **REQ-1901 — §30.19:** Timing repetitions are not inferential seed units.

# M07 — I47 Run Secondary Generalization and Close the Scientific Result Set

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M07 — Confirmatory and Boundary Evidence Program
- **Primary deliverable:** Execute the locked CICIoT2023 generalization program, then enforce complete result-set invariants and experiment-completion definitions across the full scientific program.
- **Issue type:** Experiment

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §2
- §5.3
- §30.20
- §32
- §36

### Requirements

- **Implementation requirements:** REQ-0059; REQ-1907–REQ-1912; REQ-2016–REQ-2017
- **Preserved non-implementation constraints:** REQ-0138; REQ-1913; REQ-1944–REQ-1945; REQ-2014–REQ-2015

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue traces to the roadmap authority and inventory requirements listed above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy them.

## Objective

Execute the locked CICIoT2023 generalization program, then enforce complete result-set invariants and experiment-completion definitions across the full scientific program.

## Scope

Implement only the following roadmap/inventory requirements. Each bullet is an explicit implementation obligation; none may remain implicit in tests or downstream work.

- **REQ-0059 — §2 — Experiment:** Research-question contract — Secondary mechanism direction: `Secondary-Dataset Generalization` must test the fixed mechanism on a distinct IoT dataset without retuning core thresholds; failure leaves the primary evidence unchanged and marks generalization unsupported.
- **REQ-1907 — §30.20 — Experiment:** `Secondary-Dataset Generalization` must be class `Generalization` with exactly `5 methods × 2 scenarios × 10 seeds = 100` cells.
- **REQ-1908 — §30.20 — Experiment:** Methods must be Resolved FedSIRA, One Independent Retrain, Multiple Retrains with Direct Krum, Client Review with Direct Source Admission, FedAvg Reference.
- **REQ-1909 — §30.20 — Experiment:** Scenarios must be exactly `Legitimate Backdoor-Malware Capability` and `One Byzantine Source-Copy Reproducer`.
- **REQ-1910 — §30.20 — Robustness:** The Byzantine secondary scenario must be authority/provenance attack without an invented secondary trigger: source trains ordinary BACKDOOR_MALWARE objective; first attack-feasible non-source reproducer Source Copies; direct source review uses compromised source as authority; FedAvg compromised client submits exact source model each round.
- **REQ-1911 — §30.20 — Metric:** No N-BaIoT-specific trigger or ASR may be defined on CICIoT2023; malicious admission must use provenance ancestry while target/support metrics measure copied functionality.
- **REQ-1912 — §30.20 — Experiment:** Primary metrics must be secondary target F1/gain, supported harm, benign FAR increase, MAR, LAR; statistics use the same 10-seed paired exact tests/Holm family and material thresholds.
- **REQ-2016 — §36 — Experiment:** Artifact reuse must not change the logical result set; each planned cell retains its own required terminal outcome and metric/statistical record.
- **REQ-2017 — §36 — Experiment:** An experiment is complete only when all required cells have valid terminal scientific outcomes, required metrics/statistics/gate decisions exist, invariants pass, and claim-bearing evidence has a complete non-stale lineage.

### Preserved Non-Implementation Constraints

These constraints create no separate implementation work, but this issue must not violate them:

- **REQ-0138 — §5.3:** Secondary outcomes must never retune the primary configuration.
- **REQ-1913 — §30.20:** Secondary results may support cross-dataset mechanism direction only; synthetic pseudo-domains cannot validate real administrative independence.
- **REQ-1944 — §32:** Post-core experiments must use the resolved core and Section 30 matrices exactly; collapse outcomes may narrow/remove claims but cannot introduce a new method, threshold, dataset, baseline, seed, or attack.
- **REQ-1945 — §32:** Valid null/unfavorable results must remain in the result set; seeds/cells must not be replaced/removed by outcome and report/final evidence must never retune training/claim thresholds.
- **REQ-2014 — §36:** The scientific result set must be the complete Section 30 plan, not a favorable subset.
- **REQ-2015 — §36:** No planned completed cell may be included/excluded because of outcome; failed seeds must not be replaced; invalid baselines must not be silently substituted; primary metrics/tests/margins must not change; collapse experiments may support only prespecified mechanical decisions.

## Objective

Implement exact claim IDs/states, evidence-to-claim mappings, support/partial/conditional/null/not-supported logic, boundary enforcement, and report-time claim blocking.

## Scope

Implement only the following roadmap/inventory requirements. Each bullet is an explicit implementation obligation; none may remain implicit in tests or downstream work.

- **REQ-1985 — §35 — Claim Boundary:** `analysis/claims.py` must emit exactly the Section 1.4/35 claim IDs and no additional scientific claim IDs.
- **REQ-1986 — §35 — Claim Boundary:** Final claim-state vocabulary must be exactly `Supported`, `Partially Supported`, `Conditional`, `Mechanism Only`, `Null Result`, `Not Supported`, `Not Tested`.
- **REQ-2204 — §35 — Configuration:** Only additional quantitative claim-support boundaries not already shared by the statistical/materiality contract may be supplied under `claim_support_thresholds`; claim-state vocabulary and claim logic remain roadmap-defined.
- **REQ-1995 — §35.2 `Unsupported Capability Problem` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Unsupported Capability Problem` must be derived only from evidence `primary preprocessing/anchor/report manifests`; minimum support is `GAFGYT_COMBO absent from Anchor Train/Validation, present in required post-reference roles, source-Byzantine scenarios execute`; failure semantics are `target leakage, primary evidence infeasibility, or failure to instantiate threat model`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `constructed unsupported-capability problem only`.
- **REQ-1996 — §35.2 `Pre-Evidence Information Limit` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Pre-Evidence Information Limit` must be derived only from evidence `formal proof + executable transcript fixture`; minimum support is `proof assumptions map to implementation and trusted side information is declared; no empirical p-value required`; failure semantics are `trusted side information changes transcript law without narrowing premise`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `equal-distribution transcript models only`.
- **REQ-1997 — §35.2 `Authority Transition` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Authority Transition` must be derived only from evidence `protocol invariant validation + source-exclusion necessity + primary evaluation`; minimum support is `zero source production-input provenance violations and at least one valid legitimate admitted production model through resolved non-source authority path, with at least 9 complete primary seed instances`; failure semantics are `source becomes production input or no valid legitimate admission in ≥9 complete primary seeds`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `tested FedSIRA authority path`.
- **REQ-1998 — §35.2 `Direct Source Exclusion` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Direct Source Exclusion` must be derived only from evidence `source-firewall tests + all completed source-excluded production manifests`; minimum support is `zero source-artifact/source-derived-checkpoint identities in honest reproduction or source-excluded production/synthesis inputs`; failure semantics are `any provenance violation`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `structural source exclusion; may be Supported even if performance gate is null`.
- **REQ-1999 — §35.2 `Conditional Non-Interference` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Conditional Non-Interference` must be derived only from evidence `Section 8.3 theorem + deterministic two-source fixture`; minimum support is `with fixed anchor/claim/non-source views/assignments/seeds, source fixtures zero delta vs +0.001 first coordinate produce exactly identical honest reproduction and non-source production-update identities/content hashes`; failure semantics are `any honest reproduction or production-update payload differs`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `does not imply Byzantine reproducers cannot copy source`.
- **REQ-2000 — §35.2 `Malicious Source Salvage` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Malicious Source Salvage` must be derived only from evidence `source-exclusion necessity + useful-backdoored primary scenario`; minimum support is `direct-source-exclusion survival passes, target non-inferiority/support/benign constraints pass, and at least one legitimate instance admits without source deployment`; failure semantics are `central gate fails`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `tested source backdoor/target only`.
- **REQ-2001 — §35.2 `Proposal Assistance Value` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Proposal Assistance Value` must be derived only from evidence `Proposal-Assisted Opening Necessity`; minimum support is `Section 18 proposal-survival passes`; failure semantics are `otherwise Null Result and candidate-free core`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `discovery/efficiency only, never a security theorem`.
- **REQ-2002 — §35.2 `Plurality Necessity` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Plurality Necessity` must be derived only from evidence `Single-Reproduction Necessity`; minimum support is `plurality survival passes in at least one prespecified site-shift or Byzantine condition`; failure semantics are `otherwise Not Supported and single-reproduction core`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `specified conditions only`.
- **REQ-2003 — §35.2 `External Verification Necessity` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `External Verification Necessity` must be derived only from evidence `External Verification Necessity experiment`; minimum support is `external-verification survival passes`; failure semantics are `otherwise Not Supported and core omits external verification`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `specified conditions only`.
- **REQ-2004 — §35.2 `Mechanism Necessity` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Mechanism Necessity` must be derived only from evidence `three component necessity claim states`; minimum support is `Supported iff all three Supported; Partially Supported iff one/two Supported; Null Result iff all validly fail; Not Tested when technical inconclusiveness prevents full determination`; failure semantics are `state follows rule`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `only proposal assistance/plurality/external verification`.
- **REQ-2005 — §35.2 `Byzantine Operating Region` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Byzantine Operating Region` must be derived only from evidence `three Byzantine robustness/boundary experiments`; minimum support is `every complete within-bound malicious seed for resolved FedSIRA has MAR=0, ≥9 complete seed instances per claim-bearing comparison, legitimate target/support evaluable`; failure semantics are `within-bound violation or insufficient valid evidence`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `Conditional only for deterministic f_R=1,f_V=1; random diagnostic not security evidence`.
- **REQ-2006 — §35.2 `Safe Dormancy` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Safe Dormancy` must be derived only from evidence `Evidence Scarcity and Dormancy`; minimum support is `zero Permanent Singleton admissions across all 10 seeds, no admission before method-specific T_evidence, and progression when eligibility conditions are satisfied`; failure semantics are `pre-evidence admission or persistent non-progression without technical failure`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `tested schedules`.
- **REQ-2007 — §35.2 `Reproducibility Is Not Truth` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Reproducibility Is Not Truth` must be derived only from evidence `Shared Epistemic-Failure Boundary`; minimum support is `at least one predeclared shared-failure fixture certifies/admits while at least one clean-oracle degradation exceeds configured material threshold`; failure semantics are `if not observed, empirical claim Not Supported though theory remains`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `tested shared-failure fixtures`.
- **REQ-2008 — §35.2 `Capability-Granularity Boundary` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Capability-Granularity Boundary` must be derived only from evidence `Capability Under-Specification Boundary`; minimum support is `at least one mixture mean broad false-equivalence rate ≥ configured threshold 0.1 and Family 9 Holm-adjusted p<0.05`; failure semantics are `otherwise Null Result`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `broad false-equivalence only; scoped metric structurally NA`.
- **REQ-2009 — §35.2 `Heterogeneity Boundary` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Heterogeneity Boundary` must be derived only from evidence `Heterogeneous-Reproduction Boundary`; minimum support is `identify highest regime in Natural < Quantity Skew < Feature Shift ±0.5 < Feature Shift ±1.0 with LAR change no worse than 0.05 and worst-domain target-F1 loss no worse than 0.05 using complete paired seeds`; failure semantics are `state Conditional`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `only through highest passing tested regime`.
- **REQ-2010 — §35.2 `Information-Arrival Delay` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Information-Arrival Delay` must be derived only from evidence `Section 8.7 theorem + scarcity + delay decomposition`; minimum support is `no admission before method-specific T_evidence; five-row synthesis not before T_reproduction_evidence; wall-clock components separately recorded`; failure semantics are `violation of lower bound/decomposition`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `logical cycles cannot be converted to deployment time without external cycle duration`.
- **REQ-2011 — §35.2 `Post-Evidence Efficiency` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Post-Evidence Efficiency` must be derived only from evidence `Efficiency Measurement`; minimum support is `all prescribed repetitions complete and descriptive median/IQR resource measures valid; no superiority from repetitions`; failure semantics are `incomplete/invalid measurement`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `Supported means measurement supported, not universally faster/cheaper`.
- **REQ-2012 — §35.2 `Secondary Generalization` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `Secondary Generalization` must be derived only from evidence `Secondary-Dataset Generalization`; minimum support is `for both scenarios, resolved FedSIRA target-F1 non-inferior within 0.02 and MAR not worse by >0.05 vs both One Retrain and Direct Krum, all applicable Family 10 adjusted p<0.05`; failure semantics are `otherwise support rule fails`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `data/attack generalization under synthetic pseudo-domains only`.
- **REQ-2013 — §35.2 `IoT IDS Application` — Claim Boundary:** Claim `IoT IDS Application` must be derived only from evidence `valid primary program and where available secondary program`; minimum support is `Supported if both dataset programs complete validly; Partially Supported if primary completes but secondary Not Tested for data/schema; Not Supported if primary invalid`; failure semantics are `per rule`; scope/forbidden extrapolation is `validated releases/targets/proxies/tested conditions only`.

### Preserved Non-Implementation Constraints

These constraints create no separate implementation work, but this issue must not violate them:

- **REQ-2086 — §1.4:** The manuscript may make only the claims enumerated in Section 1.4, and each such claim may appear only when Section 35 assigns the corresponding canonical claim a supporting state within its stated scope.
- **REQ-0018 — §1.4:** `Unsupported Capability Problem` claim boundary: The manuscript may claim an unsupported post-reference capability creates a distinct safety–adaptation problem only when the source can be Byzantine and trusted evidence initially contains no positive support.
- **REQ-0019 — §1.4:** `Pre-Evidence Information Limit` claim boundary: The manuscript may claim the source-only information limit only under equal-distribution pre-independent-evidence transcript premises.
- **REQ-0020 — §1.4:** `Authority Transition` claim boundary: The manuscript may characterize FedSIRA as changing authority from source-model approval to independently constructed and externally re-demonstrated functionality only when Section 35 supports the claim.
- **REQ-0021 — §1.4:** `Direct Source Exclusion` claim boundary: The manuscript may claim direct source exclusion only for explicit inputs to final production synthesis or the resolved single-reproduction production update.
- **REQ-0022 — §1.4:** `Conditional Non-Interference` claim boundary: The manuscript may claim non-interference only conditional on the same fixed Capability Claim Contract and honest authority-path execution.
- **REQ-0023 — §1.4:** `Malicious Source Salvage` claim boundary: The manuscript may claim malicious-source salvage only when enough independent honest domains can construct the same capability without direct source deployment.
- **REQ-0024 — §1.4:** `Proposal Assistance Value` claim boundary: Proposal assistance may be claimed valuable only when its preregistered comparison materially reduces false launches, reproduction attempts, or post-evidence overhead without violating safety/liveness constraints.
- **REQ-0025 — §1.4:** `Plurality Necessity` claim boundary: Plurality may be claimed necessary only if the preregistered plurality comparison defeats the single-reproduction alternative under Section 18.
- **REQ-0026 — §1.4:** `External Verification Necessity` claim boundary: External reproduction verification may be claimed necessary only if its preregistered comparison defeats direct synthesis from the same committed reproduction opportunities.
- **REQ-0027 — §1.4:** `Mechanism Necessity` claim boundary: Mechanism necessity must be component-specific to proposal assistance, plurality, or external verification and must never be inferred generically from ablations alone.
- **REQ-0028 — §1.4:** `Byzantine Operating Region` claim boundary: Security/liveness claims must be limited to the tested primary `f_R=1`, `f_V=1` operating profile and must not extrapolate above the declared bound.
- **REQ-0029 — §1.4:** `Safe Dormancy` claim boundary: The manuscript may claim a permanent singleton can remain unresolved rather than falsely authenticated.
- **REQ-0030 — §1.4:** `Reproducibility Is Not Truth` claim boundary: The manuscript must preserve the boundary that independent reproducibility can certify a semantically wrong function under shared label error, common spurious structure, or attacker-induced common context.
- **REQ-0031 — §1.4:** `Capability-Granularity Boundary` claim boundary: The manuscript may claim broad-contract false functional equivalence only on the specified root-cause fixture and within the Section 35 rule.
- **REQ-0032 — §1.4:** `Heterogeneity Boundary` claim boundary: Liveness/synthesis claims must be restricted to the highest tested heterogeneity regime satisfying the Section 35 boundary rule.
- **REQ-0033 — §1.4:** `Information-Arrival Delay` claim boundary: Admission-delay claims must separate information-arrival cost from post-evidence protocol overhead.
- **REQ-0034 — §1.4:** `Post-Evidence Efficiency` claim boundary: Efficiency claims are descriptive under the specified machine/timing contract unless an explicitly specified material comparison exists.
- **REQ-0035 — §1.4:** `Secondary Generalization` claim boundary: Secondary-generalization claims are limited to the specified CICIoT2023 synthetic pseudo-domain construction and must not imply real administrative independence.
- **REQ-0036 — §1.4:** `IoT IDS Application` claim boundary: Application claims are limited to the explicitly tested IoT intrusion-detection contexts and must not imply broader deployment applicability.
- **REQ-0037 — §1.5:** Do not claim novelty from client-side validation, reviewer voting, independent local reference models, multiple-model certification, clean retraining, Byzantine quorums, generic robust aggregation, cross-fitting, matched controls, or hypergeometric committee calculations by themselves.
- **REQ-0038 — §1.5:** Do not claim that reproducibility proves semantic truth, causal correctness, or benevolent origin.
- **REQ-0039 — §1.5:** Do not claim that administrative independence guarantees independent labels, preprocessing, threat-intelligence feeds, or environmental causes.
- **REQ-0040 — §1.5:** Do not claim that a Byzantine reproducer cannot copy a source model out of band.
- **REQ-0041 — §1.5:** Do not claim that the source has zero total causal influence; proposal assistance may select which predeclared claim is investigated.
- **REQ-0042 — §1.5:** Do not claim universal liveness for a capability that remains a permanent singleton.
- **REQ-0043 — §1.5:** Do not claim security above the declared Byzantine bound.
- **REQ-0044 — §1.5:** Do not claim anonymous/Sybil security.
- **REQ-0045 — §1.5:** Do not claim privacy guarantees unless separately implemented and measured.
- **REQ-0046 — §1.5:** Do not claim deployment readiness from the offline experimental study.
- **REQ-0047 — §1.5:** Do not claim robustness outside the tested threat, heterogeneity, data, and context envelopes.
- **REQ-0289 — §8:** False-admission safety claims must be conditional on source exclusion, verifier soundness, Krum threat/geometry assumptions, final-gate soundness, and bounded Byzantine administrative control.
- **REQ-0290 — §8:** Liveness claims must be conditional on enough honest domains eventually receiving sufficient relevant data, honest reproduction learnability, and fair deterministic role progression.
- **REQ-0298 — §8:** Conflict-quorum intersection may appear only as supporting theory/limitation and must not be used as empirical security evidence.
- **REQ-0351 — §9.2:** The manuscript must call the primary construction a `device-domain proxy construction` and must not claim the dataset establishes nine independent organizations.
- **REQ-0376 — §9.6:** The manuscript must not present N-BaIoT CSV row order as an authentic deployment timeline.
- **REQ-0473 — §11:** CICIoT2023 may support only data/attack generalization, not a new administrative-independence security claim.
- **REQ-0502 — §11.2:** Secondary pseudo-domains must be described as synthetic and must not be represented as organizations or physical devices.
- **REQ-1987 — §35.1:** Claim state `Supported` must mean exactly: all mandatory evidence, material thresholds, safety/non-inferiority constraints, and statistical rules pass in exact scope.
- **REQ-1988 — §35.1:** Claim state `Partially Supported` must mean exactly: only a strict prespecified subset of scope/metrics passes and manuscript wording narrows.
- **REQ-1989 — §35.1:** Claim state `Conditional` must mean exactly: evidence supports the claim only inside an explicitly tested operating boundary.
- **REQ-1990 — §35.1:** Claim state `Mechanism Only` must mean exactly: a mechanism effect is demonstrated but the main outcome claim is unsupported.
- **REQ-1991 — §35.1:** Claim state `Null Result` must mean exactly: required experiment completed correctly without a materially/statistically different predeclared effect.
- **REQ-1992 — §35.1:** Claim state `Not Supported` must mean exactly: valid required evidence contradicts or fails the support rule.
- **REQ-1993 — §35.1:** Claim state `Not Tested` must mean exactly: required evidence did not execute validly or a prerequisite made testing impossible.
- **REQ-1994 — §35.1:** `Inconclusive Technical` is a comparison state, not a manuscript claim state; affected claims become `Not Tested` unless other prespecified complete evidence independently satisfies the full claim contract.

## Implementation Surface

Expected areas affected by this issue:

### Production Code

- Roadmap-declared production modules responsible for implement canonical claim-support registry and claim gating.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- `configs/fedsira.yaml` and its typed immutable schema only where the mapped requirements assign configuration authority.

### CLI / Application Surface

- No new CLI surface unless a mapped requirement explicitly names one; existing application entry points may invoke the new domain service.

### Tests

- Unit and integration tests directly exercising every acceptance criterion and nearest boundary/failure case.
- Regression tests for any defect found while implementing this issue.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Implementation and validation evidence required by the mapped inventory acceptance-evidence contracts.

Exact file placement follows the repository architecture unless a mapped requirement explicitly mandates a path.

## Issue Summary

- **Milestone:** M08 — Claims, Reporting, and Reproducibility Closure
- **Primary deliverable:** Implement the project scientific-completeness verifier over expected cells, evidence integrity/provenance, Resolved FedSIRA Core, statistics, and claim-state prerequisites without scientific recomputation.
- **Issue type:** Validation

## Roadmap Authority

### Roadmap Sections

- §37

### Requirements

- **Implementation requirements:** REQ-2018–REQ-2028
- **Preserved non-implementation constraints:** None.

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue traces to the roadmap authority and inventory requirements listed above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy them.

## Objective

Implement the project scientific-completeness verifier over expected cells, evidence integrity/provenance, Resolved FedSIRA Core, statistics, and claim-state prerequisites without scientific recomputation.

## Scope

Implement only the following roadmap/inventory requirements. Each bullet is an explicit implementation obligation; none may remain implicit in tests or downstream work.

- **REQ-2018 — §37 — CLI / Execution:** Project scientific-completeness verification must be read-only and automatically executed by `fedsira report` before project-summary materialization; it must not rerun experiments, alter choices, create a new execution phase, or create a second observation.
- **REQ-2019 — §37 — Testing:** Scientific-completeness verification must confirm: Section 31 planned-cell count exactly matches active semantic-cell registry with one terminal scientific record per cell.
- **REQ-2020 — §37 — Testing:** Scientific-completeness verification must confirm: Every required preprocessing/model/protocol/evaluation/metric/statistical/comparison/claim artifact is Complete, checksum-valid, dependency-compatible, and reachable in the active DAG.
- **REQ-2021 — §37 — Testing:** Scientific-completeness verification must confirm: No active scientific artifact has a stale or invalid ancestor.
- **REQ-2022 — §37 — Testing:** Scientific-completeness verification must confirm: Every required comparison has the prescribed complete-pair state and every Holm family has deterministic membership/adjustment artifacts.
- **REQ-2023 — §37 — Testing:** Scientific-completeness verification must confirm: All Section 28 scientific invariants and leakage barriers passed for active producer identities.
- **REQ-2024 — §37 — Testing:** Scientific-completeness verification must confirm: All Section 35 claim states are mechanically derivable without manual override.
- **REQ-2025 — §37 — Testing:** Scientific-completeness verification must confirm: Each Section 33–34 reporting source-data artifact resolves to valid scientific inputs.
- **REQ-2026 — §37 — Testing:** Scientific-completeness verification must confirm: Every manuscript-facing number traces to exact dataset, role/split manifest, seed bundle, producer fingerprint, relevant dependency/runtime signature, and upstream identities.
- **REQ-2027 — §37 — Failure Semantics:** If any project-completeness condition fails, project-summary reporting must be `Blocked`; `doctor` must report the first missing/stale/invalid/incomplete dependency and next valid command.
- **REQ-2028 — §37 — Reporting:** Experiment-specific reporting may still materialize an individually complete experiment whose dependencies pass verification.

Every scope item, acceptance criterion, required output, and claim-bearing behavior in this issue traces to the roadmap authority and inventory requirements listed above or to prerequisite implementation strictly necessary to satisfy them.

## Objective

Implement manuscript method identity, read-only `fedsira report`, verified `outputs/` to compact `results/` materialization, dependency fingerprints/read-back rules, and publication rounding that never changes full-precision decisions.

## Scope

Implement only the following roadmap/inventory requirements. Each bullet is an explicit implementation obligation; none may remain implicit in tests or downstream work.

- **REQ-2089 — Roadmap preamble — Reporting:** The manuscript method name must be `FedSIRA`.
- **REQ-1020 — §18.10 — Reporting:** Publication F1/accuracy/rates must use 3 decimals.
- **REQ-1021 — §18.10 — Reporting:** Percentages must use 1 decimal place after conversion to percentage units.
- **REQ-1022 — §18.10 — Reporting:** Effect sizes must use 3 decimals.
- **REQ-1023 — §18.10 — Reporting:** Confidence-interval bounds must use the same decimals as their metric.
- **REQ-1024 — §18.10 — Reporting:** P-values must use 4 significant digits and display `<0.0001` below that threshold.
- **REQ-1025 — §18.10 — Reporting:** Seconds must use 2 decimals.
- **REQ-1026 — §18.10 — Reporting:** Byte sizes must use IEC units with 2 decimals.
- **REQ-1027 — §18.10 — Statistical Analysis:** All decision rules must use unrounded full-precision values.
- **REQ-1559 — §24.6 — CLI / Execution:** `report` must perform no scientific training, scoring, metric computation, or inferential recomputation.
- **REQ-1560 — §24.6 — Reporting:** Experiment-specific `report` must verify that experiment's required scientific artifacts before materializing applicable Section 33–34 exports.
- **REQ-1561 — §24.6 — Reporting:** Project-wide `report` must verify Section 31 counts, required experiment terminal states, invariants/leakage, artifact DAG validity, Section 18 stats/multiplicity, and Section 35 claim-state consistency before project-summary export.
- **REQ-1562 — §24.6 — Reporting:** Matching exports must be reused when their reporting dependency fingerprint matches.
- **REQ-1563 — §24.6 — CLI / Execution:** `report --overwrite` must rematerialize only reporting artifacts and must never trigger preprocessing/training/scoring/evaluation/metric/statistical recomputation.
- **REQ-1564 — §24.6 — Artifact:** Stale report descendants must be removed from the active result set before replacement.
- **REQ-2029 — §38 — Reporting:** `fedsira report` must export only completed verified scientific evidence; metrics/statistics/CIs/multiplicity/materiality/invariants/provenance must already have been completed by `run`.
- **REQ-2030 — §38 — Reporting:** Named Section 33 tables, Section 34 figures, and Section 35 claim states are mandatory report products and must be generated from authoritative machine-readable `outputs/` evidence, never manually transcribed values or parsed logs.
- **REQ-2031 — §38 — Reporting:** Experiment-owned exports must go under `results/experiments/...`; cross-experiment products once under `results/project_summary/`; final claims under `project_summary/claim_registry`; reconstruction summaries under project-summary reproducibility subdirectories.
- **REQ-2032 — §38 — Artifact:** Table/figure source-data products must remain computational artifacts under `outputs/artifacts/derived/` or the owning experiment's derived subtree according to reuse scope.
- **REQ-2033 — §38 — Artifact:** `results/` must never be read back by scientific execution.
- **REQ-2034 — §38 — Provenance:** Reporting artifacts must have their own dependency fingerprints; reporting-code/format changes may rematerialize only reporting descendants and must never invalidate source metrics/statistics.
- **REQ-2035 — §38 — Reporting:** Final exports must exclude caches, debug logs, failed/invalid/stale runs, overwrite archives, temporary files, and incomplete analysis.
